creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 11, item 2.

A missing key gives a clean RAD20041, but a `null` in the middle of a JSON path crashes with a Go stack trace:

```rad
json = [{"n": "a", "d": null}, {"n": "b", "d": {"t": 1}}]
N = json[].n
T = json[].d.t
rad json:
    fields N, T
```

```
Bug! Unhandled type for TypeAsString: <nil>
...
github.com/amterp/rad/core.TypeAsString({0x0, 0x0})
```

API responses do this often (optional detail objects that are null on most rows). Expected: treat it like a missing value (null for that row, or RAD20041), never a panic. The reporter worked around it with per-column comprehensions and `??`.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: core/json_algo.go:67 builds a "Expected map at ..., got %s" error with TypeAsString(data), and TypeAsString (core/utils.go:72) has no nil case. The type-mismatch error would also be wrong for null; null should probably yield null.
title: A JSON path that meets null partway through panics
